latest.title: How I Built a Multi-Tenant AI Agent Platform on Aurora PostgreSQL
latest.description: Starting with local PostgreSQL taught me that persistent, durable storage is the difference between a demo and a product. Here's how Aurora's Row-Level Security, pgvector, advisory locks, and bulk upsert turned Signals 4 Sales into a production-grade multi-tenant SaaS.

latest.title: Building Lore and Abyss: A Streaming AI Dungeon Crawler with Next.js, DynamoDB, and Multi-Agent AI
latest.description:
What happens when you combine modern AI agents, real-time streaming, and classic text-based RPGs?

You get Lore and Abyss—an AI-powered dark fantasy roguelike that generates immersive adventures while maintaining a persistent world state across every player decision.

Rather than building another chatbot with a fantasy prompt, I wanted to create a true game engine that keeps track of inventory, health, locations, NPCs, and story progression while streaming narrative to the player in real time.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.

trending.title: Containers with Mama J: Docker, ECS, and Fargate Explained
trending.description: Containers, Docker, ECS, Fargate. You've heard the terms, but what do they actually mean? I sat down with my mom (Mama J) to explain containers from absolute zero. In this post, I walk through the "it works on my machine" problem, what containers are, how to build one with Docker, why you need orchestration, and how Amazon ECS and Fargate let you run containers at scale without managing servers. If Mama J can get it, you can too.
